authoredSolutions.31: In ammoniacal medium \(Ni^{2+}\) gives a characteristic rosy-red precipitate with dimethylglyoxime, so it is a standard identification test for \(Ni^{2+}\) — Statement I is true. Dimethylglyoxime is bidentate, but on coordinating it loses one \(O\text{-}H\) proton per ligand and binds as a uninegative (monoanionic) ligand, not a neutral one, so Statement II is false. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.32: The carbylamine reaction converts a primary amine, on warming with \(CHCl_3\) and alcoholic \(KOH\), into a foul-smelling isocyanide. With aniline the product is phenyl isocyanide, \(C_6H_5NC\). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.34: Lyophilic (hydrophilic) sols are reversible, are not coagulated easily, and are self-stabilised without added electrolyte, so those statements are true. But because the dispersed phase interacts strongly with water, their viscosity is much higher than that of water, not of the same order — so that statement is FALSE. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.35: Steam gives carbon monoxide with red-hot coke (\(C + H_2O \rightarrow CO + H_2\), water gas), with methane (\(CH_4 + H_2O \rightarrow CO + 3H_2\), steam reforming) and with propane (\(C_3H_8 + 3H_2O \rightarrow 3CO + 7H_2\)). It does not produce \(CO\) on reacting with \(CO_2\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.36: Ethylene glycol first esterifies with oxalic acid; on strong heating to \(210^\circ C\) the glycol oxalate undergoes elimination, expelling \(CO_2\) and \(H_2O\) to give ethene, \(CH_2=CH_2\), as the major product. The oxidised products glycolaldehyde and glyoxal, and the unstable enol vinyl alcohol, are not formed. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.38: Protonation of the terminal double bond of \(CH_3CH(NO_2)CH=CH_2\) by \(H_2SO_4\) follows Markovnikov's rule, generating a secondary carbocation at the internal carbon. Benzene attacks this carbocation (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) to give \(C_6H_5CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)NO_2\), 2-nitro-3-phenylbutane. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.39: The ethyl group cannot be introduced directly (Friedel-Crafts alkylation rearranges and over-alkylates), so it is built by acylation then reduction: \(CH_3COCl/AlCl_3\) gives acetophenone and \(Zn\text{-}Hg/HCl\) (Clemmensen) reduces it to ethylbenzene. The o,p-directing ethyl group then sends \(Br_2/AlBr_3\) to the para position (4-bromo) and \(HNO_3/H_2SO_4\) to the ortho position (2-nitro). The correct order is acylation, reduction, bromination, nitration. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.42: Maltose consists of two D-glucose units joined by a \(C_1\text{-}C_4\) \(\alpha\)-glycosidic linkage. In the \(\alpha\)-anomer the free anomeric \(O\text{-}H\) on the reducing-end glucose points downward (the \(\alpha\) orientation). The structure showing the \(\alpha\)-1,4 linkage with the reducing-end anomeric \(OH\) in the \(\alpha\) position is option (D).
authoredSolutions.43: With \(H_2/CO\) over a rhodium catalyst the alkene undergoes hydroformylation (the oxo process): \(H\) and \(CHO\) add across the double bond. For 1-butene the major product is the straight-chain aldehyde pentanal, \(CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CHO\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.44: Carboxylic acids are far more acidic than phenol, so (I) phenol is the weakest. Among the benzoic acids, the electron-withdrawing \(-NO_2\) group (II, 4-nitrobenzoic acid) increases acidity, while the electron-donating \(-CH_3\) group (IV, 4-methylbenzoic acid) decreases it relative to benzoic acid (III). The order of acid character is II > III > IV > I. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.45: \(SF_4\) has a see-saw geometry (trigonal bipyramidal with one equatorial lone pair) in which the two axial \(S\text{-}F\) bonds are longer than the two equatorial \(S\text{-}F\) bonds, so its bond lengths are unequal. \(XeF_4\) (square planar), \(SiF_4\) and \(BF_4^-\) (both tetrahedral) all have equivalent bonds. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.46: The \(\alpha\) (rhombic) and \(\beta\) (monoclinic) forms of sulphur interconvert reversibly about the transition temperature of \(369\ K\) on slow heating or cooling, so Statement I is true. At room temperature the stable crystalline form is rhombic (\(\alpha\)) sulphur, not monoclinic, so Statement II is false. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.47: Nitration of aniline with \(HNO_3/H_2SO_4\) does occur. Although partial protonation to the meta-directing anilinium ion produces an appreciable amount of the meta isomer, the para isomer p-nitroaniline (A) is still formed as the major product. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.49: Natural rain water is weakly acidic with a \(pH\) of about \(5.6\) due to dissolved \(CO_2\) forming carbonic acid, so Statement I is true. When oxides of sulphur and nitrogen lower the \(pH\) below \(5.6\) the rain is termed acid rain, so Statement II is also true. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.69: The ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1\) has \(e=\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}}=\frac{3}{5}\) and foci at \((\pm 3,0)\). The hyperbola passes through these foci with transverse axis along the \(x\)-axis, so \(\frac{9}{A^2}=1\) gives \(A^2=9\). With the product of eccentricities one, \(e_{h}=\frac{5}{3}\), and \(\frac{25}{9}=1+\frac{B^2}{9}\) gives \(B^2=16\). The hyperbola is \(\frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{16}=1\). Hence option (B).
